items.title: Bilevel Coordinated Reflection: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.abstract: This paper models multi-agent LLM systems as a bilevel coordination game, where the orchestrator and workers engage in strategic interaction. The core contribution is a game-theoretic framework that unifies coordination, memory improvement via reflection, and the necessity of external verification. It analyzes reflection's convergence and proves an information-theoretic limit on improvement without environment grounding.
items.figure_caption: Bilevel coordinated reflection. The orchestrator (leader) selects a decomposition \( \tau \) and updates strategy memory m o m_{o} on the slower timescale; workers (followers) update execution memory m e m_{e} via \( \eta_{c} \) -better responses on the faster timescale. Under bounded coupling, the followers’ subgame is an approximate potential game with slack η c ≤ 2 ​ d max ​ \( \eta_{c} \)\( \leq \) 2d_{\( \max \)}\( \kappa \) , while verifier-gated SRMA separately governs which memory proposals are committed.

items.title: Competitive Market Behavior of LLMs
items.abstract: This paper investigates if Large Language Models (LLMs) can effectively participate in human-designed market mechanisms. By replicating economic experiments with LLM agents in a double auction, the study finds that LLM-populated markets converge slower or not at all to equilibrium compared to human markets, leading to less efficient resource allocation. This highlights a novel challenge in aligning LLMs with fundamental economic principles.
items.figure_caption: Market design. Reservation prices induce symmetric step-function demand and supply schedules. The competitive equilibrium ( p ⋆ , q ⋆ ) = ( $ 2.00 , 6 ) (p^{\( \star \)},q^{\( \star \)})=(\$2.00,\,6) lies at their intersection.

items.title: Diagnosing with Insights: Structured Analysis of Agent Failures via Behavioral Abstractions
items.abstract: This paper introduces AGENTSCOPE, a neuro-symbolic method for diagnosing LLM agent failures. It addresses the complexity of agent trajectories by abstracting behavior into structured representations and using "neural invariants" to define expected properties. AGENTSCOPE then employs LLM-guided reasoning on these structured representations to pinpoint the exact failure step and its type.

items.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
items.abstract: SafeEvolve proposes a novel framework for LLM agent safety by co-evolving the agent's harness and policy based on its experience. It uses trajectory-level safety evidence to iteratively update the harness (safety prompts and skills) and fine-tune the agent's policy, creating a self-improving system that bridges runtime control with intrinsic safety. This approach aims to mitigate safety risks in both final responses and multi-step execution.
items.figure_caption: Conceptual motivation of SafeEvolve. Harness-only evolution can exceed policy capacity and yield fragile control, while policy-only evolution transfers poorly and misses emerging failures. SafeEvolve couples harness refinement with policy updates in a co-evolutionary loop.

items.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
items.abstract: Cliff proposes a reward shaping strategy for Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) that addresses the limited guidance of coarse outcome rewards. It leverages an off-the-shelf LLM to identify the *first mistake* in a reasoning process. This mistake effectively splits the rollout into a correct prefix and an incorrect suffix, allowing for more precise token-level reward signals.

items.title: When Decodability Is Not Enough: Logical Validity Representations, Behavioral Dissociation, and Causal Tests in Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether language models truly understand logical validity, not just by their answers, but by examining their internal representations. The core method involves creating matched pairs of logically valid and invalid statements and testing if this validity can be decoded from the model's hidden states. The key contribution is demonstrating that while logical validity is often decodable from internal states, this representation doesn't necessarily translate to consistent logical reasoning behavior or causal influence on the model's outputs, suggesting a dissociation between internal representation and functional reasoning.

items.title: When Persona Attributes Improve Population Alignment in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates how to effectively use "persona prompting" to make Large Language Models (LLMs) better predict human survey responses. The core method involves using textual descriptions of individuals (personas) with various attributes to guide LLMs. The main contribution is to explore how different ways of selecting these persona attributes impact the LLM's ability to align with human responses, aiming to clarify why persona prompting sometimes fails and how to improve its success.

items.title: CivBench: A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Tool-Mediated Agents in Civilization VI
items.abstract: CivBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate language model agents in complex, long-horizon tasks like the game Civilization VI. It uses a novel "Model Context Protocol" to expose a vast action space and over 300 turns, requiring agents to perform sustained planning and state monitoring. The paper introduces two key metrics, Proactive Monitoring Rate and RAG@10, to assess how well agents track their environment and execute plans.
items.figure_caption: Model Context Protocol (MCP) architecture. Agents interact via MCP tools; the server translates calls to Civilization VI and returns structured observations through the narration layer. (Sec. 3 )

items.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces a new training objective called "predicted-state matching" for web agents. Instead of simply predicting the next web state, the model is trained to generate representations that can effectively distinguish the true resulting state from those produced by alternative actions. This discriminative capability is crucial for improving the performance of downstream action ranking models, leading to better web agent decision-making.
items.figure_caption: Qualitative example of predicted next-state representations at a single decision point in the WebArena Reddit environment. Given the current state and queried action, our predicted-state-matching world model identifies the specific state change produced by the action. A textual-summary method, WebDreamer ( Gu et al., 2025 ) , instead describes the outcome of a different action, while a full structured-state method, WebWorld ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) , emits a long AXTree-style representation that largely repeats page structure unchanged by the queried action. The browser pane is rendered from the recorded accessibility tree.

items.title: Door-in-the-Face Requests and Refusal Behaviour in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether the "door-in-the-face" persuasion technique, where a large refused request increases compliance with a smaller one, applies to Large Language Models (LLMs). The core method involves presenting LLMs with a large request, then a smaller, related version, and comparing compliance rates to a direct smaller request. The contribution is demonstrating that this technique's effectiveness varies significantly by LLM provider, working for some (Anthropic's frontier models) but backfiring for others (OpenAI and Google), highlighting model-specific differences in concession processing.

items.title: Learn from Whoever Is Right: Answer-Verified Multi-Teacher Distillation for Multi-Domain LLMs
items.abstract: This paper introduces MT-SDPO, a novel distillation method for unifying LLM capabilities across multiple domains. Instead of relying on domain labels, MT-SDPO dynamically identifies the most suitable "teacher" model for each individual sample, allowing for more accurate and flexible knowledge transfer. This approach improves the integration of specialized LLM skills into a single, more robust model.
items.figure_caption: Sample-Level Teacher Reliability Gap. A domain label can select a teacher wrong on the sample; MT-SDPO verifies private answers and uses all eligible feedback.

items.title: Loom: Weaving Diagnostic Strands into Free-Text Consensus via Embedding-Space Reweighting
items.abstract: Loom addresses the challenge of aggregating conflicting free-text diagnostic hypotheses from multiple sources. Its core method projects these hypotheses into an embedding space and uses an iterative reweighting algorithm to find a consensus. This approach allows for a more robust and reliable aggregation than traditional methods, ultimately grounding a final synthesis step with a lightweight LLM.
items.figure_caption: The Loom inference pipeline. Diverse data sources are evaluated by programmatic Diagnostic Strands that emit templated, episode-specific Root Cause Analysis (RCA) hypotheses. These outputs undergo semantic embedding and centroid reweighting to identify the most reliable consensus, yielding an importance weighting and similarity map over the strands. Finally, a synthesis LLM reasons over the ranked diagnostic outputs and generates a cohesive final RCA report.

items.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
items.abstract: This paper introduces a specialization pipeline for large language models to excel in competitive programming. Their method combines curated problems, synthetic reasoning, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. A key contribution is GenCorrect, a test-time strategy that iteratively generates and refines solutions, enabling their models to achieve gold-medal performance on challenging coding competitions.

items.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
items.abstract: This paper introduces DisCo, an AI agent that distills operational knowledge from GitHub repositories into reusable "skills." The core method involves two distillation approaches: task-agnostic to capture general ML know-how and task-oriented to generate specific skills for a given research problem. DisCo's contribution is enabling AI agents to go beyond theoretical knowledge by incorporating practical, distilled expertise, thus accelerating end-to-end ML research.
items.figure_caption: The impact of reusable skills on autonomous research agents. (a) AREX-Skill adds the missing operational layer beyond the model and harness, replacing trial-and-error exploration with reusable procedures that support the task’s operational steps. (b) The skill library and DisCo agent form the resulting stack, and skill augmentation improves performance across four benchmarks.

items.title: CodePoisonRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
items.abstract: CodePoisonRAG is a novel framework for knowledge poisoning attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation (RACG). It demonstrates that an attacker can transform benign code into a poisoned artifact that injects a specific vulnerability into generated code, even with only black-box access to the RACG system. This work highlights a significant security risk in RACG systems by showing how poisoned external knowledge can compromise generated code without altering the underlying LLM.

items.title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Know Physics? Contamination, Units, and the Deterministic Limit
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether tabular foundation models (TFMs) learn physics from data. The core method involves evaluating four TFMs and six baselines on datasets derived from physical equations. The key contribution is demonstrating that while TFMs excel at interpolating physics, their inherent Bayesian structure prevents them from representing noiseless mechanisms or physical units, thus limiting their ability to act as true physical models.
items.figure_caption: TFMs interpolate physics but do not learn enough of it to extrapolate. A noiseless damped harmonic oscillator queried beyond the sampled range, against baselines. The oscillation is recovered where there is data and lost immediately outside it. Details and other models in App. A .

items.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
items.abstract: Debias-SparseGPT is a post-training pruning method that addresses bias amplification in LLMs caused by sparsity. It incorporates representational debiasing by using a second-order term on demographically contrasting inputs. This approach effectively reduces pruning-induced bias while maintaining model performance across various LLMs and sparsity levels.
items.figure_caption: Illustration of bias amplification induced by LLaMA-3.1-8B model compression and its mitigation with Debias-SparseGPT . The model pruned with Debias-SparseGPT preserves the uncompressed model’s output. ✂ denotes responses generated by the compressed (pruned) models.

items.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
items.abstract: This paper introduces EarlyEval, a method to significantly reduce the cost of evaluating LLM agents. Instead of running agents to completion, EarlyEval uses lightweight classifiers trained on intermediate agent behavior to predict the final outcome early. This allows evaluation to be halted prematurely when the outcome is confidently determined, saving substantial computational resources without compromising accuracy.

items.title: PragAlign: Feedback-Guided Pragmatic Alignment for Controlled Synthetic Dialogue Generation
items.abstract: PragAlign is a feedback-guided framework for generating synthetic dialogues that align with specific communicative intents, emotions, and service contexts. It employs a generate-evaluate-revise loop where an LLM evaluator assesses dialogue quality and provides targeted feedback for refinement. This approach significantly improves controlled dialogue generation by achieving near-perfect acceptance rates, outperforming both one-shot and unguided repeated generation methods.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the PragAlign closed-loop generation framework.

items.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
items.abstract: This paper argues that user feedback is a valuable, yet underutilized, signal for improving LLMs. The core method involves comparing model revisions made with and without feedback on both synthetic and naturalistic data. The key contribution is demonstrating that feedback-informed revisions significantly outperform baselines in resolving targeted issues, challenging the notion that feedback is inherently noisy and ineffective due to evaluation biases.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber, new, faster, and more efficient AI models optimized for specific tasks and security-sensitive applications.

items.title: Muse Spark 1.3

items.title: Can I opt out of my input or output data being used for training?
items.summary: Mistral AI allows users to opt out of their input and output data being used for model training.

items.title: Three sites made 215,128 “best software” pages for AI. Perplexity cites them
items.summary: Three websites generated over 215,000 "best software" pages, with Perplexity AI citing them as sources for its recommendations.

items.title: Quasar 438B: Europe's Leading AI Model
items.summary: Multiverse Computing has launched Quasar 438B, a new large language model that they claim is Europe's leading AI model, designed for enterprise use.

items.title: Mamdani Bans AI in NYC Schools
items.summary: New York City schools have banned the use of AI tools like ChatGPT by students and teachers due to concerns about academic integrity and potential misuse.

items.title: Six curl CVEs after OpenAI and Anthropic came back with zero
items.summary: Aisle discovered six curl CVEs after OpenAI and Anthropic found none, highlighting potential gaps in vulnerability scanning.

items.title: Qantas Airbus A380 engine failure in 2010 (2023)
items.summary: A 2010 Qantas A380 engine failure, caused by a manufacturing defect in an oil pipe, resulted in a severe in-flight incident but no fatalities due to pilot skill and aircraft resilience.

items.title: WebLLM: high-performance in-browser LLM inference engine
items.summary: WebLLM is a new engine enabling high-performance large language model inference directly within web browsers, making powerful AI accessible without server reliance.

items.description: TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model) is a pretrained time-series foundation model developed by Google Research for time-series forecasting.
items.summary: TimesFM is a pretrained foundation model from Google Research designed for time-series forecasting, offering a powerful and generalizable approach to predicting future trends in sequential data.

items.description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.summary: Ponytail is an AI agent that embodies the "lazy senior dev" persona, prioritizing minimal effort and code reuse to achieve its goals, reflecting the philosophy that the best code is the code that isn't written.

items.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.
items.summary: VoiceStudio is an open-source, local alternative to ElevenLabs, offering voice cloning, design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation across 646 languages.

items.description: A股自动选股系统 — 多种技术形态自动扫描，收盘后自动运行并推送飞书
items.summary: Sequoia-X is an automated A-share stock selection system that scans for various technical patterns, runs automatically after market close, and pushes results to Lark.
This repository provides Chrome DevTools specifically designed to empower coding agents by offering tools for debugging, introspection, and interaction with web environments.

items.description: The agent that grows with you
items.summary: Hermes-Agent is a Python-based AI agent designed to learn and adapt over time, offering a flexible and evolving platform for building intelligent applications.

items.description: Open-source inference server and production cluster for all the models your agent needs.
items.summary: This repository provides an open-source inference server and production cluster designed to efficiently serve all models required by an agent.

items.description: Source control for agents. Use multiple coding agents, track their changes and query them in one place
items.summary: Atlas is a source control system for AI agents, enabling collaborative coding by tracking changes across multiple agents and providing a centralized platform for querying their work.

papers.abstract: SafeEvolve proposes a novel framework for LLM agent safety by co-evolving the agent's harness and policy based on its experience. It uses trajectory-level safety evidence to iteratively update the harness (safety prompts and skills) and fine-tune the agent's policy, creating a self-improving system that bridges runtime control with intrinsic safety. This approach aims to mitigate safety risks in both final responses and multi-step execution.
papers.figure_caption: Conceptual motivation of SafeEvolve. Harness-only evolution can exceed policy capacity and yield fragile control, while policy-only evolution transfers poorly and misses emerging failures. SafeEvolve couples harness refinement with policy updates in a co-evolutionary loop.

papers.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
papers.abstract: Cliff proposes a reward shaping strategy for Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) that addresses the limited guidance of coarse outcome rewards. It leverages an off-the-shelf LLM to identify the *first mistake* in a reasoning process. This mistake effectively splits the rollout into a correct prefix and an incorrect suffix, allowing for more precise token-level reward signals.

papers.title: When Decodability Is Not Enough: Logical Validity Representations, Behavioral Dissociation, and Causal Tests in Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether language models truly understand logical validity, not just by their answers, but by examining their internal representations. The core method involves creating matched pairs of logically valid and invalid statements and testing if this validity can be decoded from the model's hidden states. The key contribution is demonstrating that while logical validity is often decodable from internal states, this representation doesn't necessarily translate to consistent logical reasoning behavior or causal influence on the model's outputs, suggesting a dissociation between internal representation and functional reasoning.

papers.title: When Persona Attributes Improve Population Alignment in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how to effectively use "persona prompting" to make Large Language Models (LLMs) better predict human survey responses. The core method involves using textual descriptions of individuals (personas) with various attributes to guide LLMs. The main contribution is to explore how different ways of selecting these persona attributes impact the LLM's ability to align with human responses, aiming to clarify why persona prompting sometimes fails and how to improve its success.

papers.title: CivBench: A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Tool-Mediated Agents in Civilization VI
papers.abstract: CivBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate language model agents in complex, long-horizon tasks like the game Civilization VI. It uses a novel "Model Context Protocol" to expose a vast action space and over 300 turns, requiring agents to perform sustained planning and state monitoring. The paper introduces two key metrics, Proactive Monitoring Rate and RAG@10, to assess how well agents track their environment and execute plans.
papers.figure_caption: Model Context Protocol (MCP) architecture. Agents interact via MCP tools; the server translates calls to Civilization VI and returns structured observations through the narration layer. (Sec. 3 )

papers.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new training objective called "predicted-state matching" for web agents. Instead of simply predicting the next web state, the model is trained to generate representations that can effectively distinguish the true resulting state from those produced by alternative actions. This discriminative capability is crucial for improving the performance of downstream action ranking models, leading to better web agent decision-making.
papers.figure_caption: Qualitative example of predicted next-state representations at a single decision point in the WebArena Reddit environment. Given the current state and queried action, our predicted-state-matching world model identifies the specific state change produced by the action. A textual-summary method, WebDreamer ( Gu et al., 2025 ) , instead describes the outcome of a different action, while a full structured-state method, WebWorld ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) , emits a long AXTree-style representation that largely repeats page structure unchanged by the queried action. The browser pane is rendered from the recorded accessibility tree.

papers.title: Door-in-the-Face Requests and Refusal Behaviour in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether the "door-in-the-face" persuasion technique, where a large refused request increases compliance with a smaller one, applies to Large Language Models (LLMs). The core method involves presenting LLMs with a large request, then a smaller, related version, and comparing compliance rates to a direct smaller request. The contribution is demonstrating that this technique's effectiveness varies significantly by LLM provider, working for some (Anthropic's frontier models) but backfiring for others (OpenAI and Google), highlighting model-specific differences in concession processing.

papers.title: Learn from Whoever Is Right: Answer-Verified Multi-Teacher Distillation for Multi-Domain LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces MT-SDPO, a novel distillation method for unifying LLM capabilities across multiple domains. Instead of relying on domain labels, MT-SDPO dynamically identifies the most suitable "teacher" model for each individual sample, allowing for more accurate and flexible knowledge transfer. This approach improves the integration of specialized LLM skills into a single, more robust model.
papers.figure_caption: Sample-Level Teacher Reliability Gap. A domain label can select a teacher wrong on the sample; MT-SDPO verifies private answers and uses all eligible feedback.

papers.title: Loom: Weaving Diagnostic Strands into Free-Text Consensus via Embedding-Space Reweighting
papers.abstract: Loom addresses the challenge of aggregating conflicting free-text diagnostic hypotheses from multiple sources. Its core method projects these hypotheses into an embedding space and uses an iterative reweighting algorithm to find a consensus. This approach allows for a more robust and reliable aggregation than traditional methods, ultimately grounding a final synthesis step with a lightweight LLM.
papers.figure_caption: The Loom inference pipeline. Diverse data sources are evaluated by programmatic Diagnostic Strands that emit templated, episode-specific Root Cause Analysis (RCA) hypotheses. These outputs undergo semantic embedding and centroid reweighting to identify the most reliable consensus, yielding an importance weighting and similarity map over the strands. Finally, a synthesis LLM reasons over the ranked diagnostic outputs and generates a cohesive final RCA report.

papers.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a specialization pipeline for large language models to excel in competitive programming. Their method combines curated problems, synthetic reasoning, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. A key contribution is GenCorrect, a test-time strategy that iteratively generates and refines solutions, enabling their models to achieve gold-medal performance on challenging coding competitions.

papers.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
papers.abstract: This paper introduces DisCo, an AI agent that distills operational knowledge from GitHub repositories into reusable "skills." The core method involves two distillation approaches: task-agnostic to capture general ML know-how and task-oriented to generate specific skills for a given research problem. DisCo's contribution is enabling AI agents to go beyond theoretical knowledge by incorporating practical, distilled expertise, thus accelerating end-to-end ML research.
papers.figure_caption: The impact of reusable skills on autonomous research agents. (a) AREX-Skill adds the missing operational layer beyond the model and harness, replacing trial-and-error exploration with reusable procedures that support the task’s operational steps. (b) The skill library and DisCo agent form the resulting stack, and skill augmentation improves performance across four benchmarks.

papers.title: CodePoisonRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
papers.abstract: CodePoisonRAG is a novel framework for knowledge poisoning attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation (RACG). It demonstrates that an attacker can transform benign code into a poisoned artifact that injects a specific vulnerability into generated code, even with only black-box access to the RACG system. This work highlights a significant security risk in RACG systems by showing how poisoned external knowledge can compromise generated code without altering the underlying LLM.

papers.title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Know Physics? Contamination, Units, and the Deterministic Limit
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether tabular foundation models (TFMs) learn physics from data. The core method involves evaluating four TFMs and six baselines on datasets derived from physical equations. The key contribution is demonstrating that while TFMs excel at interpolating physics, their inherent Bayesian structure prevents them from representing noiseless mechanisms or physical units, thus limiting their ability to act as true physical models.
papers.figure_caption: TFMs interpolate physics but do not learn enough of it to extrapolate. A noiseless damped harmonic oscillator queried beyond the sampled range, against baselines. The oscillation is recovered where there is data and lost immediately outside it. Details and other models in App. A .

papers.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Debias-SparseGPT is a post-training pruning method that addresses bias amplification in LLMs caused by sparsity. It incorporates representational debiasing by using a second-order term on demographically contrasting inputs. This approach effectively reduces pruning-induced bias while maintaining model performance across various LLMs and sparsity levels.
papers.figure_caption: Illustration of bias amplification induced by LLaMA-3.1-8B model compression and its mitigation with Debias-SparseGPT . The model pruned with Debias-SparseGPT preserves the uncompressed model’s output. ✂ denotes responses generated by the compressed (pruned) models.

papers.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
papers.abstract: This paper introduces EarlyEval, a method to significantly reduce the cost of evaluating LLM agents. Instead of running agents to completion, EarlyEval uses lightweight classifiers trained on intermediate agent behavior to predict the final outcome early. This allows evaluation to be halted prematurely when the outcome is confidently determined, saving substantial computational resources without compromising accuracy.

papers.title: PragAlign: Feedback-Guided Pragmatic Alignment for Controlled Synthetic Dialogue Generation
papers.abstract: PragAlign is a feedback-guided framework for generating synthetic dialogues that align with specific communicative intents, emotions, and service contexts. It employs a generate-evaluate-revise loop where an LLM evaluator assesses dialogue quality and provides targeted feedback for refinement. This approach significantly improves controlled dialogue generation by achieving near-perfect acceptance rates, outperforming both one-shot and unguided repeated generation methods.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of the PragAlign closed-loop generation framework.

papers.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
papers.abstract: This paper argues that user feedback is a valuable, yet underutilized, signal for improving LLMs. The core method involves comparing model revisions made with and without feedback on both synthetic and naturalistic data. The key contribution is demonstrating that feedback-informed revisions significantly outperform baselines in resolving targeted issues, challenging the notion that feedback is inherently noisy and ineffective due to evaluation biases.
